# Separator — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a separator when a boundary between two runs of content would otherwise be invisible: between sections of a menu, above a footer, between a form's groups. It is a rule, not a spacer — if the two things are separate enough to need a line, they are usually separate enough to be two sections with their own headings. Keep separators few; a list where every row is divided is a list where the divider has stopped meaning anything.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a separator when two things need dividing and the division is visual rather than semantic: a break in a toolbar, a rule between list groups. It is a `View` with an `orientation`, and that is the whole component. Note what it is not: a separator is decoration between content, not a heading. If the division names what follows, that is a heading or a group label, and a line alone will not tell anyone where one section ends and the next begins.
